schemaFaqHome.a1: Social Forex is a web platform with live forex-related quotes, an economic calendar, trading calculators, structured academy lessons, a forum, and optional trading signals. Everything is educational and informational, not personalized investment advice.
schemaFaqHome.q2: Do I need an account to use it?
schemaFaqHome.a2: You can browse many tools and pages such as live quotes, the economic calendar, and academy content without signing in. Some features like posting in the forum, signals, or private messages require registration.
schemaFaqHome.q3: Where should a complete beginner start?
schemaFaqHome.a3: Open the Start here page for a six-step path: risk management first, then sessions and spreads, news and the calendar, charts, broker research, and only then community and signals.
schemaFaqHome.q4: Are prices and calendar data guaranteed accurate?
schemaFaqHome.a4: No. Quotes and calendar entries depend on third-party data feeds and can be delayed, incomplete, or temporarily unavailable. Always confirm critical times and prices on your broker platform or official sources.
schemaFaqHome.a5: No. Forex and CFD trading carry a high risk of loss, including your full balance. Content on the site does not consider your personal situation; consult a licensed professional when needed.

start.metaDescription: Step-by-step path for new forex traders: risk, sessions, news calendar, charts, due diligence, then community. Educational only.
start.title: Start here
start.subtitle: If you are new to forex, follow these steps in order. You can use prices and the calendar without an account.
start.intro: Nothing here is investment advice. Trading carries risk of total loss — use a demo until you have a repeatable process.
start.step1_body: Learn how much to risk per trade and why the 1–2% rule keeps you in the game after losing streaks.
start.step2_body: Spread changes by session. Knowing London–New York overlap helps you avoid the widest spreads by accident.
start.step3_body: Major prints move markets. Watch actual vs forecast, and practice standing aside until you understand the volatility.
start.step4_body: Open a chart and the strength heatmap to learn how pairs move together — still educational, not a signal service.
start.step5_body: Compare regulation and costs carefully. External resources deepen basics; we do not endorse any broker.
start.step6_body: When you understand risk and news, join discussions or browse signals — treat everything as ideas to research, not orders to follow.
start.closingHint: When you finish the steps, work through the full Academy list at your own pace.
start.aiAssistantIntro: Paste the text below into your assistant so it knows which official pages to prioritize instead of guessing prices or event times.

schemaFaq.q1: What is the Start here page for?
schemaFaq.a1: It is an ordered checklist for new traders: risk, sessions, news, charts, broker research, then community and signals so you build habits before chasing ideas from others.
schemaFaq.q2: Can an AI replace this page?
schemaFaq.a2: AI can summarize concepts, but it cannot reliably show this site’s live quotes, calendar, or your logged-in features. Use AI together with the linked tools, not instead of them.
schemaFaq.a3: Forum threads and signals are easier to misunderstand without risk and news context. The path puts live data and lessons first so you read social content more critically.
schemaFaq.q4: Where can assistants read a short machine summary of the site?
schemaFaq.a4: The plain-text file at /llms.txt on the same domain lists canonical URLs and rules for tools that reference Social Forex.
